newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends mixed on October expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends mixed on October expiry.

text.p: The NYMEX oil complex ended mixed Monday as traders unraveled their positions in the expiring October refined products contract and took profits in crude after a top U.N. aide expressed hope for the Iraq "oil-for-food" deal.
"There was expiration-related selling in refined products, and news that the humanitarian aide for Iraq may get going took crude lower," said William Brown, president of W.H. Brown & Co.
October gasoline ended down 1.89 cents a gallon to 62.71 cents.

October heating oil ended a mere 0.02 cent higher at 71.51 cents a gallon as traders rolled over their positions into the November contract. Heating oil prices were volatile as tight supplies have made prices resilient during market weakness.

November crude hit a contract high of $24.80 a barrel, but it settled 22 cents lower at $24.38 after United Nations Under Secretary General Yasushi Akashi said he hoped the Iraq oil-for-food deal could go ahead in the near future.
Akashi told a news conference in Geneva Monday that the world body was assessing whether all conditions had been met for the suspended deal to be implemented.

Heating oil stocks are 18 million barrels below a year ago, but the U.S. Energy Information Administration said Monday that heating supplies should be sufficient to meet demand this winter, which further pressured refined product prices.
"That was an excuse to sell the market," a trader said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
